description: A six-channel mono mixer with a three-band equaliser, two effect sends and a pan on every channel, and stereo returns for both effects

params.text: Sets that channel's level into the main mix, from silence to 6dB above unity
Places that channel in the stereo picture, equal power, centred in the middle of its travel
Sets how much of that channel goes to the A send, from silence to 6dB above unity; it is taken after the equaliser and before the level and pan, so it does not follow the fader
Sets how much of that channel goes to the B send, from silence to 6dB above unity; it is taken after the equaliser and before the level and pan, so it does not follow the fader
Sets how much of the A return goes into the main mix, from silence to 6dB above unity
Sets how much of the B return goes into the main mix, from silence to 6dB above unity
Sets the level of the whole mix, from silence to 6dB above unity, applied after the returns are added
Steps that channel through muted, soloed and normal on each press; its lamp is red while muted and blue while soloed
Cuts or lifts everything below 250Hz on that channel, from -12dB to 12dB
Cuts or lifts a band centred on 700Hz on that channel, from -12dB to 12dB
Cuts or lifts everything above 2000Hz on that channel, from -12dB to 12dB

inputs.text: The signal into that channel; an unpatched channel is skipped entirely and costs nothing
One side of the stereo return from effect A; with only one of the pair patched it feeds both sides
One side of the stereo return from effect A; with only one of the pair patched it feeds both sides
One side of the stereo return from effect B; with only one of the pair patched it feeds both sides
One side of the stereo return from effect B; with only one of the pair patched it feeds both sides

outputs.text: One side of the main stereo mix
One side of the main stereo mix
The sum of every channel's A send, mono
The sum of every channel's B send, mono

notes: soloing any channel silences every channel that is not soloed.
a polyphonic cable into a channel is summed to mono and divided by the square root of its channel count, so a sixteen-voice chord arrives at about the level of one voice.
the effect returns are added after the main mix is scaled and before the MAIN LEVEL knob, so they escape auto scaling but not the main level.
the lamp columns are levels over 30dB: eight steps for each side of each effect return, and fifteen for each side of the main output.
if one of the equaliser filters ever produces a value that is not a number, that stage is reset and passes its input through unchanged for that sample.
menu: Auto scale main out — divides the channel mix by the square root of how many channels are playing, so adding channels does not push the main output up; the effect returns are not scaled
